source_text: Sequitur vero Sapientia: Quis tibi imputabit si perierint nationes, quas tu fecisti, cum non sit alius Deus, quam tu, cui cura est de omnibus? Sed cum sis iustus, iuste omnia disponis; ipsum quoque qui non debet puniri, condemnare, exterum aestimas a tua virtute; virtus enim tua iustitiae initium est [n209] . Astipulatur certe communi prudentum rationi, quia maximum in Deo signum iustitia sit, quam Manichaeus, et Traducianus omni conatu fabularum suarum pernegat.
pass_a_gloss: But Wisdom follows: Who will impute to you if the nations which you made have perished, since there is no other God than you, whose care is of all? But since you are just, you dispose all things justly; even to condemn him who ought not to be punished you estimate foreign from your virtue; for your virtue is the beginning of justice. He certainly agrees with the common reason of the prudent, that the greatest sign in God is justice, which Manichaeus and the Traducian by every attempt of their fables utterly deny.

lemmas.lexica: Julian's polemic label for teachers of tradux peccati
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Wisdom continues: “Who will accuse you if nations you made perish, when there is no other God besides you, who cares for all? But since you are just, you order all things justly. You consider condemning someone who should not be punished foreign to your power, for your power is the beginning of justice” (Wisdom 12:12–16). This certainly agrees with the common reasoning of sensible people that justice is the greatest mark of God—a justice that Manichaeus and the advocate of inherited sin deny with every effort of their fables.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)
